h1: Meter Bank Replacement for Apartment Buildings in Broward County
intro: When a meter bank fails, a whole apartment building can go dark at once. The meter bank is the row of sockets feeding every apartment, so when it corrodes, burns, or is damaged, the whole building can lose power together. Our largest recent job was a ten-meter bank replaced after a vehicle fire, back online within two weeks and the electrical work done in one. We show up whenever you call.

definition.heading: What a meter bank is and why it matters
definition.body: A meter bank is the ganged assembly of meter sockets serving a multi-unit building, one per apartment. Because every unit runs through it, the bank is a shared point of failure that can darken many units at once when it corrodes, overheats, or is damaged. Decades of South Florida heat, humidity, and salt air corrode the metal that carries the load.

symptoms.title: Multiple units lost power at once
symptoms.body: Several apartments, or the whole building, went dark together while the neighborhood still has power. When many units fail at the same time, the fault is usually at the shared service or the meter bank, not inside any single unit.

symptoms.title: Rust and corrosion across the bank
symptoms.body: The bank shows rust streaks, pitting, or chalky corrosion spreading across the enclosure and sockets. Salt air and humidity eat at the metal that carries every tenant's load, and widespread corrosion means the whole bank is aging out.

symptoms.title: Scorching, heat, or a burning smell
symptoms.body: Scorch marks, melted spots, or a hot plastic smell anywhere on the bank mean connections are arcing under load. On a shared assembly feeding many units, that is a serious fire risk that needs a licensed electrician right away.

symptoms.title: Damaged service after an impact or fire
symptoms.body: A vehicle strike, fire, storm damage, or vandalism has physically damaged the service equipment or meter bank. When the assembly is compromised, the building may be unsafe and dark until it is properly replaced, which is work we handle.

localSections.heading: Aging apartment stock and original service
localSections.body: A large share of Broward County's rental housing dates to the 1960s through the 1980s and still runs on original service equipment. Meter banks installed when the building went up have carried load through decades of South Florida summers, unit after unit. Metal fatigues, jaws loosen, and connections work loose, and on an apartment building that decline sits above every tenant.

localSections.heading: Heat, humidity, and salt air on a shared assembly
localSections.body: The climate that wears a single socket is even harder on a bank, with more positions, connections, and exposed metal. Near the coast, salt air corrodes the enclosure, jaws, and lugs, and the cooling load runs most of the year. Heat drives corrosion, corrosion adds resistance, and resistance makes more heat, so equipment here can fail across several positions at once.

guide.title: The complete guide to meter bank replacement for South Florida apartment buildings

sections.heading: A real job: ten meters back online in a week
sections.body: An apartment building lost power for a week after a vehicle fire damaged the meter bank feeding the units, a crisis with tenants losing air conditioning and refrigeration. We took on the ten-meter socket bank replacement, coordinated the utility and permit, and finished the electrical work in one week, back online within two weeks. Every situation differs and the site visit comes first, but that is the scale and speed we handle.

sections.heading: Why meter banks fail on older buildings
sections.body: Corrosion leads, since the assembly lives outdoors in constant humidity and coastal salt air settles into every jaw and lug. Heat is next, from the climate and the current itself; corroded connections add resistance, resistance makes heat, and heat speeds corrosion. Add decades of age and sudden events like a strike, fire, or storm, and a bank fails broadly, not at one meter, so replacement is often the honest answer.

sections.heading: How a replacement is planned, with the utility and permit
sections.body: Replacing a bank on an occupied building starts with a thorough assessment of every position and the service, so we know exactly what to replace. Because the meters belong to the power company, the work runs in order: a scheduled disconnect, the licensed replacement with climate-rated equipment, inspection, then reconnect. Service-side work is permitted in Broward County, and we manage the whole chain while keeping the outage as short as safety allows.

faqs.question: The whole building lost power. Is that the meter bank?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. If many units or the entire building went dark at once while the neighborhood still has power, the fault is usually at the shared service or the meter bank, not inside any single unit. We come out, confirm where the failure is, and tell you honestly whether it is a targeted repair or a full bank replacement.

faqs.question: How long will tenants be without power?
faqs.answer: The building is off during the replacement and the utility disconnect and reconnect, so we plan that window to be as short as safety allows and communicate the timing clearly. The exact length depends on the size of the bank, what we find, and the utility scheduling, all of which we walk through before the work day.

faqs.question: Do you handle the power company and the permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. A bank replacement requires coordinating the utility disconnect and reconnect, pulling the permit, and passing inspection. We manage all of it under our license and meet the inspector in person, so you handle tenants and the owner while we handle the utility and paperwork.

faqs.question: Should I repair one bad meter position or replace the bank?
faqs.answer: It depends on the assembly. If corrosion, heat damage, or age is spread across the bank, replacing one position just moves the problem, and on older buildings the whole assembly is often at the end of its life. We assess the full bank and the service, then give a straight recommendation, and if a targeted repair will genuinely hold, we tell you that too.
